hook: You stop smelling your own kitchen after a few minutes. A faint star vanishes when you look straight at it. Soup tastes like nothing when your nose is blocked. Each of these is a clue to how your senses turn light, sound, chemicals and pressure into the signals your brain reads.

prereq.why: The occipital lobe, at the back, processes visual information.

prereq.q: What does the thalamus do with signals from the senses?
options: Relays them to the right areas of the cortex
prereq.why: The thalamus relays signals from every sense except smell to the cortex.

figure.caption: The eye: light is focused on the retina, where rods and cones transduce it. Tap "Hide labels" to test yourself.

chain.cause: Energy (light, sound waves, chemicals, pressure) reaches a sense organ
chain.effect: receptor cells transduce it into neural signals

chain.cause: The signal must be strong enough
chain.effect: it is detected at or above the absolute threshold; a change is noticed only above the just-noticeable difference (Weber's law)

chain.cause: A stimulus stays the same for a while
Signals travel to the brain (most through the thalamus)
chain.effect: the brain codes color, pitch, taste and pain, explained by trichromatic and opponent-process, place and frequency, and gate control theories

ideas: Sensation starts with transduction. The absolute threshold is the faintest stimulus detected half the time; the just-noticeable difference grows with the stimulus (Weber's law: a constant proportion). Signal detection theory adds expectations and stakes.

Vision: rods (dim light, no color, around the edge) and cones (color, detail, packed in the fovea). Color: trichromatic theory (three cone types) and opponent-process theory (paired processes; afterimages).

Hearing: hair cells in the cochlea. Place theory explains high pitches, frequency theory low ones, the volley principle in between. Conduction deafness: outer or middle ear. Sensorineural deafness: cochlea or auditory nerve.

Chemical senses: olfaction and gustation (sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami, and oleogustus for fat). Pain: gate control theory, phantom limbs. Body: vestibular sense (balance) and kinesthesis (position).

misconception.wrong: Your eyes see everything in front of you in sharp color, all the time.
misconception.right: Only the fovea sees sharp detail and color; the edges of your vision rely on rods that see poorly in color. You also have a blind spot in each eye with no receptors. The brain fills in the gaps.

summary: Sensation is detecting energy and transducing it into neural signals. Thresholds, Weber's law and signal detection describe what we notice, and adaptation and interaction change it. Rods and cones see; trichromatic and opponent-process theories explain color. Hair cells in the cochlea hear; place, frequency and volley theories explain pitch, and hearing loss is conduction or sensorineural. Smell, taste, touch, pain, balance and body position complete the senses.
